title: Practice: constructions
intro: Ten questions on how and why constructions work. Try at least two of them for real with compasses.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for constructing a $60^\circ$ angle at X in order.

items.text: Draw a line and mark the point X on it
With centre X, draw an arc that cuts the line at A
Keeping the same width, draw an arc with centre A that cuts the first arc at Y

hints: The arc centred on A has to cross an arc that already exists.
questions.explanation: Because the compasses never change width, XA = AY = XY. Triangle XAY is equilateral, so angle YXA is $60^\circ$.

options.text: It makes an equilateral triangle, and every angle of one is $60^\circ$
A circle has $360^\circ$ and you divide by 3

hints: What do you know about the three lengths XA, AY and XY?
questions.explanation: All three sides are one compass-width long, so the triangle is equilateral and each angle is $180^\circ \div 3 = 60^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Match each angle to the quickest way to construct it.

right.text: Construct $90^\circ$, then add a $45^\circ$ next to it

questions.explanation: $60 \to 30 \to 15$ and $90 \to 45 \to 22.5$. For $135^\circ$, put $90^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ side by side (or construct $45^\circ$ and take the angle on the other side of the straight line: $180 - 45 = 135$).

questions.prompt: You can construct an angle of $20^\circ$ by bisecting angles, starting from $60^\circ$ or $90^\circ$.
hints: List what you can reach: 60, 30, 15, 7.5 … and 90, 45, 22.5 …
questions.explanation: False. Halving $60^\circ$ gives $30, 15, 7.5, \dots$ and halving $90^\circ$ gives $45, 22.5, \dots$ None of those is $20^\circ$, and adding them cannot make exactly 20 either. $20^\circ$ needs a protractor.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for constructing a perpendicular at the point X on a line in order.

items.text: With centre X, draw arcs that cut the line at A and B
Draw arcs from A and from B that cross above and below the line at P and Q

hints: The arcs from A and B need to be wider than AX, or they will not cross.
questions.explanation: P and Q are each the same distance from A as from B, so the line PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB. It passes through X at $90^\circ$.

questions.prompt: To construct the perpendicular **from a point X above a line**, what is the first step?

options.text: Draw an arc centred at X that cuts the line in two places
Measure the distance from X to the line
Draw a line through X parallel to the first line

hints: You need two points on the line that are the same distance from X.
questions.explanation: The arc gives two points on the line equally far from X. Crossing arcs from those two points, then joining X to the crossing, gives the perpendicular.

questions.prompt: Plan a construction one step at a time.
questions.scenario: You draw AB = 8 cm, construct a $90^\circ$ angle at A, and mark C on the new line so that AC = 6 cm. Then you join B to C.

steps.prompt: What kind of triangle is ABC?
When you measure BC, how long should it be?
steps.feedback: $\sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10$ cm — a quick check that your right angle is accurate.

steps.prompt: You now bisect angle BAC. What angle does the bisector make with AB?

questions.explanation: Angle BAC is $90^\circ$, so BC $= \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10$ cm, and bisecting the right angle gives $45^\circ$. If your BC is not close to 10 cm, your perpendicular was not accurate.

questions.prompt: A triangle has a 6 cm base with angles of $45^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ at its ends. Which constructions do you need?

options.text: Construct $90^\circ$ at one end, then bisect it
Construct $60^\circ$ at the other end, then bisect it
Construct the perpendicular bisector of the base

questions.explanation: $45^\circ$ comes from bisecting a right angle and $30^\circ$ from bisecting $60^\circ$. Extend the two arms until they meet to finish the triangle.

questions.prompt: You construct a $45^\circ$ angle on a straight line. What is the angle on the other side of the arm, on the same straight line?
hints: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.
questions.explanation: $180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ$. This is the easiest way to construct $135^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Flip through the constructions. Picture each one before you turn the card.

cards.back: Arc from X to A; same width, arc from A; join X to the crossing. (Equilateral triangle.)
Arc from the vertex cutting both arms; equal arcs from those two points; join the vertex to the crossing.

cards.front: Perpendicular at a point X on a line
cards.back: Arcs from X to A and B; wider arcs from A and B crossing at P and Q; join PQ.

cards.front: Perpendicular from a point X to a line
cards.back: Arc from X cutting the line twice; equal arcs from those points crossing on the far side; join X to the crossing.
Equal arcs (more than half AB) from A and from B, above and below; join the two crossings.

questions.explanation: Every one of these relies on points that are equal distances from two other points.
